content.text: {"persuasion":"UNPERSUADED","support_scope":"NONE","rationale":"The book presents a substantial case that Jonah’s whole story typologically anticipates Jesus’ passion and mission, but that broader typology does not establish its distinctive lexical claim that “the heart of the earth” means Jerusalem. Ezekiel 5:5 establishes Jerusalem as situated among surrounding nations, while Ezekiel 38:12 speaks of the center/navel of the land; neither identifies “heart of the earth” as a scriptural name for Jerusalem. The book must also shift from geographical Jerusalem to the city’s juridical or political power because Jesus was seized and buried outside its gates.
